# Barter
A social trading app built with React, TypeScript, Vite and Appwrite. Users sign
up, post items with photos, browse an infinite feed, search, save posts and edit
their profile.
## Stack
- **React 18** + **TypeScript**, bundled by **Vite 7**
- **Appwrite** (Web SDK 16) for auth, database and file storage
- **TanStack Query v4** for server state
- **Tailwind CSS** + **shadcn/ui** + **Radix UI** for the interface
- **React Hook Form** + **Zod** for form validation
## Getting started
The app expects an Appwrite project with a database containing `users`, `posts`
and `saves` collections plus a storage bucket. Copy each ID from the Appwrite
console into `.env.local`.
### Scripts
| Script | Purpose |
| `npm run dev` | Start the Vite dev server |
| `npm run build` | Typecheck, then build to `dist/` |
| `npm run preview` | Serve the production build locally |
| `npm run lint` | ESLint (flat config), zero warnings tolerated |
| `npm run format` | Prettier, including Tailwind class sorting |
## Configuration and secrets
Every variable in `.env.local` is prefixed `VITE_`, which means **Vite inlines it
into the JavaScript bundle and it is publicly readable by anyone who loads the
site**. That is expected for Appwrite's client SDK — project and collection IDs
are identifiers, not credentials.
Because the browser holds no secret, all access control has to live server-side:
- Restrict the project to your own domains under **Appwrite → Settings →
Platforms**. Without this, any origin can talk to your project using these IDs.
- Set per-collection and per-document permissions so users can only read and
write their own records.
- Never put an Appwrite **API key** in this file. API keys carry server-side
privileges and would be exposed to every visitor.
`.env.local` is gitignored. Keep it that way.
### Appwrite hardening checklist
Since the project ID is public, these console settings are what actually protect
the data. Work through them once per project:
**Settings → Platforms**
- [ ] Add a Web platform for each domain you serve from (production domain, any
Vercel preview domains, and `localhost` for development).
- [ ] Confirm there is no wildcard `*` entry. A wildcard lets any site on the
internet make authenticated requests using your project ID.
**Auth → Security**
- [ ] Set session length to something sane rather than the default year.
- [ ] Enable "Personal data" protection so user emails aren't returned in
listings.
- [ ] Turn on rate limiting for auth endpoin
